- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast peaks, especially after spikes.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or volatile, model often underestimates; increase low-range forecasts to avoid missing downward trends.
- Model frequently overreacts to short-term sentiment shifts — especially when sentiment spikes to 1.00, leading to exaggerated overshoots; apply dampening factor to forecast peaks.
- In periods of mean reversion (sentiment oscillates around 0.5), model often fails to revert — over-forecasting or under-forecasting mid-range; align forecast to historical mean of last 5–7 days.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overestimate early in the forecast window (first 5–7 days) when sentiment is neutral or slightly positive — reduce initial forecast values.
- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.33) and price is trending down, model often fails to recognize the trend — increase forecast values to reflect downward momentum.
- Model underestimates when sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67) and price is volatile — adjust forecast upward to account for sentiment uncertainty.
- Overshoots after sentiment spikes are common — apply a “cool-down” rule: reduce forecast by 15–30% after a sentiment spike to avoid overcorrection.
